fixes.explanation: Not this time, friend. The priests and diviners say the opposite: “…do not send it away empty, but by all means return it to Him with a guilt offering.” (1 Samuel 6:3) So the ark does not go back with nothing along with it.

That's it, friend. The priests and diviners tell them, “Give glory to the God of Israel, and perhaps He will lift His hand from you and your gods and your land.” (1 Samuel 6:5) So glory is part of what they're told to give. It's right there in the same breath as the gold rats.

Right, friend. The cows “…headed straight up the road toward Beth-shemesh, staying on that one highway and lowing as they went, never straying to the right or to the left.” (1 Samuel 6:12) They don't wander and they don't turn back. That's some serious commitment from two cows.

Yes, friend. The rulers of the Philistines “…followed behind them to the border of Beth-shemesh.” (1 Samuel 6:12) They follow along behind the cows instead of waiting for news. I think I'd have wanted to see it with my own eyes too.

I can see why you'd guess that, friend, since this story has had its scary moments. But the text says they “…were overjoyed at the sight.” (1 Samuel 6:13) They look up from the wheat and they're glad.

Two cows pulling a cart down the road would confuse me too, friend. But the text doesn't say they were confused. It says they “…were overjoyed at the sight.” (1 Samuel 6:13) Whatever questions they had, the joy is what the passage shows.

Not quite, friend. The text says, “…the Levites took down the ark of the LORD and the chest containing the gold objects…” (1 Samuel 6:15) The rulers followed the cows to the border of Beth-shemesh and later saw what happened (1 Samuel 6:12, 16). So the Levites are the ones who lift it down.

That's right, friend. The text says the Levites “…took down the ark of the LORD and the chest containing the gold objects, and they placed them on the large rock.” (1 Samuel 6:15) The rulers followed the cows to the border and later saw it all (1 Samuel 6:12, 16). The ark is handled by Levites.

Yes, friend. The text says, “…when the five rulers of the Philistines saw this, they returned to Ekron that same day.” (1 Samuel 6:16) They see the ark and the offerings, then they go back to Ekron. All of it happens that same day.

Yes, friend. The men of Beth-shemesh send messengers to the people of Kiriath-jearim with this message: “The Philistines have returned the ark of the LORD. Come down and take it up with you.” (1 Samuel 6:21) That's the town they ask. They don't keep it, and they send word.

Bethel is a real place in the Bible, friend (Genesis 28:19), but this passage doesn't send the ark there. The messengers go “…to the people of Kiriath-jearim…” (1 Samuel 6:21) That's the town that gets the call, and that's the town that comes.
